answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost.
